payload.title: Server-preference tie-break for every negotiator
payload.goal: Add the `{ preferred }` option, which today only encodings take, to mediaTypes/mediaType, languages/language and charsets/charset, so a server can break a tie between values the client rates equally.
acceptance: With `Accept: text/html, application/json`, `mediaTypes(['text/html', 'application/json'], { preferred: ['application/json'] })` returns `['application/json', 'text/html']`, and `mediaType` with the same arguments returns `'application/json'`.
languages/language and charsets/charset take `{ preferred }` the same way: among equal q-values the preferred value comes first.
A lower q-value still loses: with `Accept-Language: en, fr;q=0.5`, `languages(['en', 'fr'], { preferred: ['fr'] })` keeps `en` first.
Calls without the option behave as before, and the existing tests still pass.
README.md documents the option for media types, languages and charsets, as it does for encodings.

payload.text: All acceptance checks pass - now verifying existing tests still hold.

Implemented `{ preferred }` tie-break for media types, languages and charsets, mirroring encodings.

- `lib/mediaType.js`, `lib/language.js`, `lib/charset.js`: added third `preferred` param with q-first comparator; preferred only reorders equal q-values, falling back to specificity/order otherwise; matching is case-insensitive and returns provided casing.
- `index.js`: `mediaType(s)`, `language(s)`, `charset(s)` now accept `(available, options)` and forward `options.preferred`; `encodings` refactored to share the same extractor.
- `README.md`: documented `mediaType(s)`, `language(s)`, `charset(s)` with `{ preferred }` as done for encodings.

decision: preferred breaks ties only among equal q-values and never overrides q, matching the encodings comparator
decision: preferred matching is case-insensitive while returning the provided casing

findings.text: Negotiator methods call getPreferred(options) but getPreferred is not defined in the diff, causing runtime error.
preferredOrder is used without normalization; normalizePreferred is defined but never applied, so preferred option handling diverges from language/charset.
compareWithPreferred duplicated per file instead of shared, increasing drift risk.
Comparator fallback for non-preferred items uses (a.o - b.o) ordering which may differ from compareSpecs intent.
